paper.title: Perishability of Data: Dynamic Pricing under Varying-Coefficient Models

settings.name_in_paper: Feature-based dynamic pricing with varying-coefficient linear valuation model, adversarial features
unmapped: Posted-price setting: valuation v_t = <theta_t, x_t> + z_t, seller observes only binary sale/no-sale feedback, revenue p_t*1(v_t>=p_t)
Noise CDF F strictly increasing with F and 1-F log-concave; the learner knows F (uses pricing function g and the log-likelihood)
Parameters theta_t vary arbitrarily over time with variation delta_t = ||theta_{t+1}-theta_t||; regret against clairvoyant knowing theta sequence
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the market value of a product is a linear function of its covariates, namely v_t(x_t) = <theta_t, x_t>+z_t. ... If p_t <= v_t, a sale occurs, and the firm collects revenue p_t. ... The sequence of parameters theta = (theta_1,theta_2,...) is unknown to the firm and they may vary across time.

||theta_t|| <= W with W known; time-varying parameters with variation delta_t
settings.definition_quote: (Stochastic features model). Feature vectors x_t are generated independently according to a probability distribution P_x, with a bounded support in R^d. We denote by Sigma the covariance matrix ... 0<C_min/d <= sigma < C_max/d.

algorithms.name: PSGD (Projected stochastic gradient descent) pricing policy
PSGD pricing policy for stochastic features model (adaptive step sizes from empirical covariance)
requires_knowledge_of: noise CDF F (pricing function g, ell_M)

symbols.B_f: max value of noise density f
symbols.ell_M: inf over |x|<=M of min second derivatives of -log F and -log(1-F)
symbols.u_M: sup over |x|<=M of max first derivatives of -log F and -log(1-F)

conditions: Assumption 2.1: F strictly increasing, F and 1-F log-concave

source.label: thm1
source.quote: Then, the regret of PSGD pricing policy using a non-increasing sequence of step sizes $\{\eta_t\}_{t\ge1}$ is bounded as follows: \Reg(T) \le \frac{2(2B+MB')}{\ell_M} \max\bigg\{\frac{16}{\ell_M} \log T, \,\frac{2W^2}{\eta_{T+1}} + \frac{u_M^2}{2} \sum_{t=1}^T \eta_t + 2W \sum_{t=1}^T  \frac{\delta_t}{\eta_t} \bigg\}+\frac{M}{T}

results.notes: Paper's W (norm bound on theta) mapped to S. Worst case over theta in Theta and x in X; expressed in terms of variations delta_t. Dimension-free.

conditions: Assumption 2.1: F strictly increasing, F and 1-F log-concave

source.label: thm1
source.quote: In particular, if $\eta_t \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}$, then there exists a constant $C = C(B,M,W,\ell_M, u_M) >0$, independent of $T$, such that \Reg(T) \le C\Big(\sqrt{T} + \sum_{t=1}^T \sqrt{t} {\delta_t}\Big)

results.notes: Stated in text right after Theorem 3.1 as a specialization. Constant depends on B, M, W, ell_M, u_M; independent of d.

conditions: Assumption 2.1: F strictly increasing, F and 1-F log-concave
Assumption 4.1: i.i.d. features on unit ball with covariance eigenvalues in [C_min/d, C_max/d)
tuning: eta_t = 1/(lambda_t t), lambda_t = ell_M/(6t)(1+sum_{l<=t} sigma_l) with sigma_l min eigenvalue of empirical covariance

source.label: thm:log-regret
source.quote: Under the stochastic features model (Assumption~\ref{SMF}), the regret of PSGD pricing policy is bounded as follows: \Reg(T) \le C_1 d^2 \log T + C_2\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{t}{d}\delta_t, where $\delta_t \equiv \|\th_{t+1}-\th_t\|$ and $C_1, C_2$ are constants that depend on $C_{\max}, C_{\min}, u_M, \ell_M, M, B, W$ but are independent of dimension $d$.

results.notes: Constants C_1, C_2 unspecified (absorbed in O). Regret is worst case over theta and feature distributions in Q.
